literal: " Thereupon the emperor put Shou in sole charge of the task.
idiomatic: " With that the emperor gave Shou exclusive responsibility for the work.

literal: He also ordered Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi to supervise it in general, but Longzhi only appended his signature.
idiomatic: He also ordered Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi to oversee the project, though Longzhi did no more than sign his name.

literal: The emperor charged Shou, saying, "Keep a straight brush—I shall never act like Emperor Taiwu of Wei and kill the historians.
idiomatic: The emperor charged Shou, saying, "Write straight—I shall never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei did and execute the historians.

literal: " At the beginning of Wei, Deng Yanhai compiled the Records of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; afterward Cui Hao took charge of the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yan, and others in succession maintained the craft.
idiomatic: " In early Wei, Deng Yanhai compiled the Records of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; later Cui Hao directed the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yan, and others carried on the work generation after generation.

literal: Hao used the annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the book had still not appeared.
idiomatic: Hao wrote in annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, yet the book still had not been published.

literal: In the Xuanwu era the court ordered Xing Luan to compile a follow-on Daily Records of Emperor Xiaowen; the text ran to the fourteenth year of Taihe, and Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were then ordered to continue it.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu the court ordered Xing Luan to compile a Daily Records of Emperor Xiaowen; the text reached the fourteenth year of Taihe, and then Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were ordered to carry it on.

literal: It ran down to Emperor Xiaoming, and the events were set forth in great detail.
idiomatic: It continued down to Emperor Xiaoming, with events recorded in exhaustive detail.

literal: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of Distinguishing the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.
idiomatic: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of Distinguishing the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.

literal: Shou thereupon joined with Unimpeded Regular Attendant Fang Yanyou, Minister of Works Chief Clerk Xin Yuanzhi, National University Erudite Diao Rou, Pei Angzhi, and Masters of Writing Gentleman Gao Xiaogan in overall deliberation to complete the Book of Wei.
idiomatic: Shou then joined Unimpeded regular attendant Fang Yanyou, minister of works chief clerk Xin Yuanzhi, national university erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and masters of writing gentleman Gao Xiaogan in overall deliberation to finish the Book of Wei.

literal: He fixed names and titles, selected entries clause by clause, also searched out what was lost, stitched on later events, and completed the historical record of a whole dynasty, presenting it in memorial to the throne.
idiomatic: He fixed names and titles, chose entries clause by clause, recovered what had been lost, stitched on later events, and completed the historical record of a whole dynasty, then memorialized it to the throne.

literal: He brought to completion the great canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical scrolls, one hundred and ten scrolls in all.
idiomatic: He brought to completion the great canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical scrolls, one hundred and ten scrolls in all.

literal: In the third month of the fifth year it was submitted.
idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year it was submitted.

literal: In autumn he was made governor of Liang province.
idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed governor of Liang province.

literal: Because the treatises were not yet finished, Shou memorialized asking to complete the work, and permission was granted.
idiomatic: Because the treatises were still unfinished, Shou asked leave to complete them and was allowed.

literal: In the eleventh month he again submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena, four scrolls; Geography, three scrolls; Calendars and Pitchpipes, two scrolls; Rites and Music, four scrolls; Food and Goods, one scroll; Punishments, one scroll; Omens, two scrolls; Offices and Clans, two scrolls; Buddhism and Daoism, one scroll—twenty scrolls in all, continued after the annals and biographies, one hundred and thirty scrolls together, divided into twelve fascicles.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena (four scrolls), Geography (three), Calendars and Pitchpipes (two), Rites and Music (four), Food and Goods (one), Punishments (one), Omens (two), Offices and Clans (two), and Buddhism and Daoism (one)—twenty scrolls in all, appended to the annals and biographies for one hundred and thirty scrolls together, divided into twelve fascicles.

literal: The history had thirty-five topical models, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and in all two tables and one memorial besides.
idiomatic: The history had thirty-five topical models, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and besides two tables and one memorial.

literal: Of the historians he cited, fearing they might press upon him, he took only those of the scholarly current who had long relied on him.
idiomatic: Among the historians he enlisted, fearing they might crowd him, he took only scholars of his own circle who had long attached themselves to him.

literal: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang, though long involved in court posts, were none of them talents for history.
idiomatic: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang had long held court posts, yet none had a gift for history.

literal: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit to compile and edit.
idiomatic: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit for compilation.

literal: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.
idiomatic: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.

literal: The ancestors and affines of the men who revised the history were for the most part entered in the record and adorned with fine words.
idiomatic: The ancestors and affines of those who revised the history were for the most part written up and dressed in fine words.

literal: Shou's nature was rather quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne grudges against him had much of their good left out.
idiomatic: Shou was quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne him grudges found much of their merit omitted.

literal: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares show color to Wei Shou!
idiomatic: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares stand up to Wei Shou!

literal: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."
idiomatic: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."

literal: " When Shou was in Gao Huan's time Vice Director of the Imperial Clan and revised the national history, he received Yang Xiuzhi's help and therefore thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay your kindness than to write you a fine biography.
idiomatic: " In Gao Huan's day, when Shou was vice director of the imperial clan and revised the national history, Yang Xiuzhi helped him; Shou thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay you than to write you a fine biography.

literal: " Xiuzhi's father Gu in Wei times had been governor of Beiping and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by Chief Commandant of Justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.
idiomatic: " Xiuzhi's father Gu had been governor of Beiping in Wei and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by chief commandant of justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.

literal: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office for a public matter.
idiomatic: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office over a public matter.

literal: " It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him.
idiomatic: " It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him.

literal: " Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao clan sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou moreover accepted gold from Rong's son, he reduced Rong's evil and increased his good, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates the wind of virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—what are they worth counting?"
idiomatic: " Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao house sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou had also taken gold from Rong's son, he softened Rong's crimes and magnified his virtues, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—how are they worth counting?"

literal: Public opinion had already said Shou's history was unfair; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Shou to the Masters of Writing to debate jointly with the descendants of the various families; before and after, more than a hundred people submitted complaints, saying "his family's hereditary posts were left out," or saying "his family does not appear in the record," or saying "there is groundless slander."
idiomatic: Opinion already held that Shou's history was unfair; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Shou to the Masters of Writing to debate with the descendants of the various families; in all more than a hundred people complained that hereditary posts had been omitted, that their house was not recorded, or that they had been slandered without cause.

literal: " Shou answered each case as presented.
idiomatic: Shou answered each complaint as it stood.

literal: Fanyang Lu Pei's father Tong was placed under his clan grandfather Xuan's biography as an attached entry; Dunqiu Li Shu's family biography said his origin was Meng in Liang; Pei and Shu criticized it, saying, "The history is not straight.
idiomatic: Fanyang Lu Pei's father Tong was attached under his clan grandfather Xuan's biography; Dunqiu Li Shu's family biography said his line came from Meng in Liang; Pei and Shu protested that "the history is not straight.

literal: " Shou's nature being quick, he could not bear his rage and memorialized that they wished to have him slaughtered.
idiomatic: Shou, quick-tempered, could not contain his anger and memorialized that they meant to have him killed.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and personally interrogated and rebuked them.
idiomatic: The emperor was furious and personally interrogated and rebuked them.

literal: Pei said, "My father served Wei, rose to Pillar of State, his achievements were illustrious, his name known throughout the realm, and he had no kinship with Shou—yet no biography was made for him.
idiomatic: Pei said, "My father served Wei, rose to pillar of state, his achievements were illustrious and his name known throughout the realm, and he was no kin of Shou—yet no biography was made for him.

literal: Boling Cui Chuo held office only as merit officer of his home commandery and had no further deeds, yet as Shou's maternal kin he was made the lead entry of a biography.
idiomatic: Boling Cui Chuo held office only as merit officer of his home commandery and had no further deeds, yet as Shou's maternal kin he led a biography.

literal: " Shou said, "Though Chuo had no office, his reputation and conduct were admirable, and therefore he deserved a biography.
idiomatic: Shou said, "Though Chuo had no office, his reputation and conduct were admirable, and therefore he deserved a biography.

literal: " The emperor said, "How do you know he was a good man?
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "How do you know he was a good man?

literal: " Shou said, "Gao Yun once wrote a eulogy for Chuo, praising his virtue.
idiomatic: Shou said, "Gao Yun once wrote a eulogy for Chuo praising his virtue.

literal: " The emperor said, "The Minister of Works is a man of talent; when he writes a eulogy for someone, of course he should praise him.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The minister of works is a man of talent; when he writes a eulogy for someone, of course he praises him.

literal: It is just as when you write an essay for someone and speak of his good points—can they all be true?
idiomatic: It is just as when you write for someone and speak of his virtues—can they all be true?

literal: " Shou had nothing to answer and only trembled.
idiomatic: Shou had nothing to answer and only trembled.

literal: But the emperor had long valued Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.
idiomatic: But the emperor had long valued Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.

literal: At the time Taiyuan Wang Songnian also slandered the history; Pei and Shu were both punished, each flogged and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died from it; Lu Sidao was also punished.
idiomatic: At the time Wang Songnian of Taiyuan also attacked the history; Pei and Shu were both punished, flogged and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died of it; Lu Sidao was punished as well.

literal: Yet because mouths still seethed, he ordered that the Wei history for the time not be promulgated and commanded the officials to debate broadly, allowing those with family matters at stake to enter the office and submit memorials where things were untrue.
idiomatic: Yet because complaint still boiled over, he ordered the Wei history withheld for the time and commanded officials to debate broadly, allowing anyone with a family stake to enter the office and file memorials where facts were wrong.

literal: Thereupon every mouth clamored and it was called the "Foul History"; memorials poured in one after another, and Shou could not withstand them.
idiomatic: Thereupon every tongue cried out and it was called the "Foul History"; memorials poured in one after another, and Shou could not withstand them.

literal: At the time Left Vice Director Yang Yin and Right Vice Director Gao Dezheng, the two men's power tilted the court and countryside; both were close to Shou, and Shou thereupon wrote biographies for both their houses.
idiomatic: At the time left vice director Yang Yin and right vice director Gao Dezheng tilted court and countryside between them; both were close to Shou, and Shou wrote biographies for both families.

literal: The two did not wish to say the history was untrue and suppressed the complaints; through the end of the Wenxuan era it was never debated again.
idiomatic: The two would not admit the history was false and choked off the complaints; through the end of the Wenxuan reign it was never reopened.

literal: Masters of Writing Lu Cao once said to Yin, "Wei Shou's Book of Wei may be called broad in learning and great in talent, with great merit to the house of Wei.
idiomatic: Masters of writing Lu Cao once told Yin, "Wei Shou's Book of Wei is broad in learning and great in talent, with great merit to the Wei house.

literal: " Yin said to Shou, "This is a book that cannot be carved away—it will pass through ten thousand ages.
idiomatic: Yin told Shou, "This is a book that cannot be carved away—it will pass through ten thousand ages.

literal: Only I regret that in discussing the branches, leaves, and affines of the various families it is too prolix and unlike the form of the old histories.
idiomatic: Only I regret that in treating the branches, leaves, and affines of the various families it is too prolix and unlike the old histories in form.

literal: " Shou said, "Formerly, because the central plains fell into chaos, gentry genealogies were for the most part lost, and therefore I fully recorded their collateral lines.
idiomatic: Shou said, "Formerly, when the central plains fell into chaos, gentry genealogies were largely lost, and therefore I fully recorded collateral lines.

literal: I hope you will see the fault and know the kindness, and spare me severe blame."
idiomatic: I hope you will see the fault and know the kindness, and spare me severe blame."

literal: " In the summer of the eighth year he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and supervised the national history, again taking part in deliberating on statutes and ordinances.
idiomatic: " In the summer of the eighth year he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent and supervised the national history, again joining deliberation on statutes and ordinances.

literal: When the Three Terraces were completed, Wenxuan said, "When the terrace is completed there must be a fu.
idiomatic: When the Three Terraces were completed, Emperor Wenxuan said, "When a terrace is finished there must be a rhapsody.

literal: " Yin had first told Shou; Shou submitted the "Rhapsody on the New Palace and Terraces of the Imperial Residence," and its text was very grand.
idiomatic: Yin had warned Shou beforehand; Shou submitted the "Rhapsody on the New Palace and Terraces of the Imperial Residence," and its text was very grand.

literal: Of those who composed at the time, from Xing Shao downward none matched it.
idiomatic: Of those who wrote at the time, from Xing Shao downward none matched it.

literal: Several days before Shou submitted the fu he had only then told Shao.
idiomatic: Only a few days before submitting the rhapsody did Shou tell Shao.

literal: Shao afterward told others, "Shou is a very hateful man—why did he not speak sooner?
idiomatic: Shao later told others, "Shou is a hateful man—why did he not speak sooner?

literal: " The emperor once toured East Mountain and ordered Shou to draft an edict proclaiming majesty and virtue and admonishing the lands west of the passes; in a moment it was finished, and its reasoning and diction were grand.
idiomatic: " The emperor once toured East Mountain and ordered Shou to draft an edict proclaiming majesty and virtue and admonishing the lands west of the passes; in a moment it was done, and its reasoning and diction were grand.

literal: Facing the hundred officials the emperor greatly sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Facing the hundred officials the emperor sighed in great admiration.

literal: He was then also made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: He was then also made junior mentor of the heir apparent.

literal: Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, the younger sister of Cui Angzhi, and she bore one daughter but no son.
idiomatic: Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, younger sister of Cui Angzhi; she bore one daughter but no son.

literal: The granddaughters of Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang and of Secretariat Gentleman Cui Qishi, whose husbands' families had been implicated in cases, the emperor bestowed on Shou as wives; men of the time compared it to Jia Chong's setting up a left and a right madam.
idiomatic: The granddaughters of Wei grand master of ceremonies Liu Fang and of secretariat gentleman Cui Qishi, whose husbands' families had been implicated, the emperor bestowed on Shou as wives; men of the time compared it to Jia Chong keeping a left and a right madam.

literal: Yet there were still no sons.
idiomatic: Yet he still had no sons.

literal: Later, when he fell gravely ill, fearing that after his death the principal wife and concubines would not be at peace, he released the two concubines.
idiomatic: Later, when he fell gravely ill, fearing strife between principal wife and concubines after his death, he released the two concubines.

literal: When the illness abated he recalled them with longing and wrote the "Rhapsody on Longing in Separation" to express his feeling.
idiomatic: When the illness abated he recalled them with longing and wrote the "Rhapsody on Longing in Separation" to express his feeling.

literal: Wenxuan at every drunken feast would say, "The heir apparent is timid by nature; the altars of state are weighty affairs—ultimately the succession should pass to Changshan.
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan at every drunken feast would say, "The heir apparent is timid by nature; the altars of state are weighty—ultimately the succession should pass to Changshan.

literal: " Shou said to Yang Yin, "The ancients said the heir apparent is the root of the state and must not be shaken.
idiomatic: Shou told Yang Yin, "The ancients said the heir apparent is the root of the state and must not be shaken.

literal: After the August One has taken three cups, he every time speaks of passing the succession to Changshan, making his ministers doubtful and divided.
idiomatic: After His Majesty has taken three cups, he every time speaks of passing the succession to Changshan, making his ministers doubtful and divided.

literal: If it is real, it must be carried out decisively.
idiomatic: If he means it, it must be carried out decisively.

literal: If these words are in jest, Wei Shou, having the shameful post of tutor, ought rightly to guard the heir to the death—only I fear the state will not be secure.
idiomatic: If these words are in jest, Wei Shou, having the shameful post of tutor, ought to guard the heir to the death—only I fear the state will not be secure.

literal: " Yin reported Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on he stopped.
idiomatic: Yin reported Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on he stopped.

literal: The emperor often held feasts of pleasure, and Shou each time attended in attendance.
idiomatic: The emperor often held feasts of pleasure, and Shou each time attended.

literal: When the crown prince took Zheng of the good secondary consortship, the offices prepared a full set of sacrificial meats; the emperor, already deep in drink, rose and himself overturned and destroyed them.
idiomatic: When the crown prince took Zheng as good secondary consort, the offices prepared a full set of sacrificial meats; the emperor, already deep in drink, rose and overturned them himself.

literal: He then charged Shou, saying, "Do you know my intent?
idiomatic: He then charged Shou, saying, "Do you know my intent?

literal: " Shou said, "This subject foolishly thinks that since the chief secondary consort is already a concubine of the Eastern Palace, by right she needs no full victims; looking up to consider Your Sagely intent, it was on this account that you destroyed them.
idiomatic: Shou said, "This subject foolishly thinks that since the chief secondary consort is already a concubine of the eastern palace, by right she needs no full victims; looking up to Your Sagely intent, it was on this account that you destroyed them.

literal: " The emperor laughed greatly, grasped Shou's hand, and said, "You know my intent.
idiomatic: " The emperor laughed loudly, grasped Shou's hand, and said, "You know my intent.

literal: " Prince Ande Yan Zong took as consort the daughter of Li Zu of Zhao commandery; later the emperor visited the Li house for a feast, and the consort's mother Song presented two pomegranates before the emperor.
idiomatic: " Prince Ande Yan Zong took as consort the daughter of Li Zu of Zhao commandery; later the emperor visited the Li house for a feast, and the consort's mother Song presented two pomegranates before the emperor.

literal: He asked the company and none knew the meaning; the emperor tossed them aside.
idiomatic: He asked the company and none knew the meaning; the emperor tossed them aside.

literal: Shou said, "The pomegranate has many seeds within— the prince is newly wed, and the consort's mother wishes many sons and grandsons.
idiomatic: Shou said, "The pomegranate has many seeds within—the prince is newly wed, and the consort's mother wishes many sons and grandsons.

literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and charged Shou, "Bring them back," and at once bestowed on Shou two bolts of fine brocade.
idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased and charged Shou, "Bring them back," and at once bestowed two bolts of fine brocade on Shou.

literal: In the tenth year he was made Pillar of State of the third rank.
idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made pillar of state of the third rank.

literal: At a banquet the emperor orally charged that he be made Director of the Secretariat and ordered Secretariat Gentleman Li Yin to draft the edict under a tree.
idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor orally ordered him made director of the secretariat and commanded secretariat gentleman Li Yin to draft the edict under a tree.

literal: Yin, because Shou was a towering talent of an age, found it hard to compose offhand, and long went without finishing.
idiomatic: Yin, because Shou was a towering talent of an age, found it hard to compose offhand and long went without finishing.

literal: By the time it was done the emperor had sobered from wine and did not speak of it again; Yin still did not submit it, and the matter in the end lapsed.
idiomatic: By the time it was done the emperor had sobered and did not speak of it again; Yin still did not submit it, and the matter lapsed.

literal: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Shou and Zhongshan governor Yang Xiuzhi to deliberate on auspicious and inauspicious rites, and both managed edicts and charges.
idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Shou and Zhongshan governor Yang Xiuzhi to deliberate on auspicious and inauspicious rites, and both managed edicts and charges.

literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: He was then made palace attendant and promoted to director of the imperial clan.

literal: Wenxuan's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Shou's deliberations.
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Shou's deliberations.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao held affairs as regent in the center, he ordered Shou to remain within the palace to draft the various edicts and charges; for days he did not go out.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao held affairs as regent in the center, he ordered Shou to remain in the palace to draft the various edicts; for days he did not go out.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the secretariat.

literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made Concurrent Palace Attendant, Right Grand Master of the Palace, still Pillar of State, and supervisor of the histories.
idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was made concurrent palace attendant, right grand master of the palace, still pillar of state, and supervisor of the histories.

literal: Shou had earlier served as deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang and they did not get along.
idiomatic: Shou had earlier served as deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang and they did not get along.

literal: At the time Xin's younger brother Xi was intimate with the emperor.
idiomatic: At the time Xin's younger brother Xi was intimate with the emperor.

literal: But Emperor Xiaozhao separately ordered Yang Xiuzhi to hold the secretariat concurrently and at Jinyang manage edicts and charges, while Shou remained at Ye—this was Xi's doing, and Shou was greatly resentful.
idiomatic: But Emperor Xiaozhao separately ordered Yang Xiuzhi to hold the secretariat concurrently and at Jinyang manage edicts, while Shou remained at Ye—this was Xi's doing, and Shou was greatly resentful.

literal: He said to heir apparent attendant Lu Xunzu, "If you were made to compose edicts and charges, I too would say nothing.
idiomatic: He told heir apparent attendant Lu Xunzu, "If you were made to compose edicts, I too would say nothing.

literal: " He also made Zu Ting compiler in the Masters of Writing, intending that Ting replace Shou.
idiomatic: " He also made Zu Ting compiler in the Masters of Writing, intending that Ting replace Shou.

literal: Minister of Works Chief Clerk Li Zhu, a man of literary phrasing, heard it and told others, "Edicts and charges all go to Yang Zilie; compilation is again sent to Zu Xiaozheng—the literary and historical offices are suddenly lost; I fear the Duke of Wei will break out in a rash on his back.
idiomatic: Minister of works chief clerk Li Zhu, a man of letters, heard it and told others, "Edicts all go to Yang Zilie; compilation is again sent to Zu Xiaozheng—the literary offices are suddenly stripped; I fear the Duke of Wei will break out in a rash on his back.

literal: " At the time an edict debated the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests; Shou held to the interpretations of Wang Su and Du Yu, taking the Yuan and the Sima as the Two Kings and Tongcao as supplying the Three Honored Guests.
idiomatic: " At the time an edict debated the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests; Shou held to Wang Su and Du Yu, taking the Yuan and the Sima as the Two Kings and Tongcao as supplying the Three Honored Guests.

literal: The edict ordered all officials of ritual learning to hold to Zheng Xuan's doctrine of five generations.
idiomatic: The edict ordered all officials of ritual learning to hold to Zheng Xuan's doctrine of five generations.
